fatal_errors: The proposed composition-series intervention does not reconstruct the target HEBM-plus-SPS processing study or its nanocrystalline FCC/BCC structural mediator.

The cited Mo-Ti evidence shows screw-controlled strength below about 40 at% Ti and edge-dislocation strengthening becoming comparable only around 60-80 at% Ti, so it does not support a general claim that incremental Ti addition immediately governs strength through edge-dislocation barriers.
The proposed Mo-based HEA composition is unspecified, while the cited experiments concern reduced-complexity Mo-Ti solid solutions; applicability to a multicomponent HEA is therefore not established.
explanation: This is a testable alternative solid-solution-strengthening hypothesis, but it is not a reconstruction of the hidden CoCrFeNiTi powder-processing study. It omits high-energy ball milling, SPS, nanocrystalline grain refinement, milling-induced dislocation density, densification, and the 83% FCC/17% BCC phase mixture. Consequently, it does not predict the target hardness, compressive strength, density, yield stress, or fracture behavior and uses the wrong baseline. Its Ti-series design, phase checks, mechanical testing, TEM, and explicit falsification rule provide reasonable discriminability. However, grain size, texture, oxygen content, and processing history would also need to be controlled. The evidence supports a Ti-dependent misfit effect in Mo-Ti and an eventual screw-to-edge strengthening transition, but it supports edge control only at high Ti and addresses yield strength more directly than hardness. Thus the proposal is scientifically plausible but only indirectly evidenced for an actual HEA.
